en: The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom, translated by the Tripitaka Master and Śramaṇa Facheng, a Great Virtuous One of the State from the Dunhuang Grottoes.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
at that time the Blessed One entered the gateways to the Dharma known as the samādhi of Profound Clarity.

Furthermore, at that time, when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was practicing the profound perfection of wisdom, he observed and clearly perceived that the essential nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, addressed the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"If a son of good family wishes to practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), how should he further train and study?"
Having spoken these words, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara replied to the Venerable Śāriputra:

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā, they should contemplate in this way: the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty."
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.
Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form.
In this same way, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also all empty.
Therefore, Śāriputra, the emptiness of all phenomena is signless, without arising and without ceasing, stainless and free from stain, neither decreasing nor increasing. Śāriputra!
Therefore, at that time, within emptiness, there is no form, no sensation, no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness.
There is no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, and no mind.
There is no form, no sound, no odor, no taste, no touch, and no phenomena.
There is no eye-element, and so forth, up to no consciousness-element.
There is no ignorance, nor is there the end of ignorance; and so forth, up to no old age and death, nor is there the end of old age and death.
There is no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path; there is no wisdom, nothing to be attained, and likewise nothing not to be attained.

Therefore, Śāriputra, because there is nothing to be attained, the assembly of Bodhisattvas relies upon the Prajñāpāramitā; their minds are without hindrance, they have no fear, they transcend all perversions, and they reach ultimate Nirvāṇa.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time likewise, by relying upon the Prajñāpāramitā, have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Śāriputra!
Therefore, one should know that this great mantra of the Prajñāpāramitā is the great vidyā-mantra, the unsurpassed mantra, and the unequaled mantra.
The mantra that can eliminate all suffering is true and unerring.
Therefore, know that the Prajñāpāramitā is a secret mantra.
He then spoke the Prajñāpāramitā mantra, saying:
“Gatē gatē pāragatē pārasaṃgatē bodhi svāhā. Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the profound perfection of wisdom in this manner.
At that time, the World-Honored One arose from that samādhi and addressed the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Good son! It is so, it is so! It is just as you have said."
"He should train in the perfection of wisdom in this manner;
all Tathāgatas shall also rejoice in it.
When the Bhagavān had spoken these words, [the assembly rejoiced].

Venerable Śāriputra, when the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken thus, all the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others in the world heard what the Buddha had taught; they were all greatly rejoiced, and having faith, they accepted and practiced it.
The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-sūtra)
